study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Sampaio et al., Artificial Intelligence in Medicine, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: A generalizable normative deep autoencoder for brain morphological anomaly detection: application to the multi-site StratiBip dataset on bipolar disorder in an external validation framework

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study states clear objectives and the purpose of applying a normative modeling framework to characterize brain morphology in bipolar disorder, including assessing group differences, heterogeneity, and individualized deviation maps. This directly satisfies both criteria: explicit research aims and explicit purpose of using normative modeling for clinical insights.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We used deep autoencoders in an anomaly detection framework... applied to multi-site external data of HC and BD individuals. We found that brain deviating scores were greater, more heterogeneous..."; "A shift from a disease-centred to a patient-centred paradigm is promoted via the development of a generalizable, and extendable AE-based brain normative modelling and anomaly detection framework."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study builds a new normative model using the HCP-YA dataset. It cites the original HCP source, specifies the age range and that subjects are healthy controls, reports the final sample size (N=1109), and describes image quality checks (visual QC and CAT12 QC). However, specific reasons for exclusion within the HCP sample are not detailed in this paper.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Our training set was obtained from the HCP-YA public dataset... 3 T T1-weighted sMRI scans from 1109 HC subjects aged between 22 and 37 years..."; "All sMRI data were pre-processed in Matlab R2018a... T1-weighted images underwent a visual quality check... CAT12-based quality check... identifying images with an intensity covariance below two standard deviations."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates age and sex (and TIV for volumes) are explicitly modeled. Site effects are addressed via M-ComBat harmonization using HCP-YA as reference, and biological covariates are further removed by linear regression fit on HCP-YA and applied consistently. Preservation of biological covariates after harmonization is validated.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "An innovative end-to-end pipeline was designed to manage both biological and site-related confounding sources..."; "For all feature sets, age and sex were included as biocovariates to preserve, while for volume features, previously harmonized TIV was also included."; "After data harmonization, we proceeded with the removal of variance associated with age and sex... and harmonized TIV from volume features, via standard LR..."; "The reported results indicate that the biological covariates effects were totally preserved in the harmonized data..."

It also specifies the implementation libraries and versions (Keras 3.3.3, TensorFlow 2.16.1).
